fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. God says, “Once and for all I have sworn by My holiness…” Then He says, “I will not lie to David.” He swears by His own holiness, and that's about as solid as an oath gets.

Good guess, because a temple sounds like a natural spot for something that important. But Ethan never mentions a temple in this verse. He says, “in the heavens You establish Your faithfulness.” Even a really tall roof can't beat that.

Right on the money, baker. God swore, “I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all generations.” Look at who gets the promise: David, Israel's king, and the family line that follows him. That's a long-lasting oath, one that reaches well past David himself.
That's it, baker. Ethan says, “You rule the raging sea; when its waves mount up, You still them.” The waves are piling up, and the LORD stills them. That's what ruling the raging sea looks like.
You got it, baker. Ethan says, “Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at Your name.” These are two whole mountains, and they're shouting! Ethan says they do it at the LORD's name.
Correct, friend. God says, “No enemy will exact tribute; no wicked man will oppress him.” So no enemy collects tribute from David, and no wicked man oppresses him. That's what the LORD promises him.

That's right, baker. God says David's offspring shall endure forever, and his throne is “…like the moon, established forever, a faithful witness in the sky.” So the moon follows the sun in the promise. Sun and moon, both lining up with that throne.
